regimens.indication: Acute Hypotension / Septic & Neurogenic Shock (Adults — Continuous IV Infusion)

refs.quote: LEVOPHED is indicated to raise blood pressure in adult patients with severe, acute hypotension. LEVOPHED is a catecholamine indicated for restoration of blood pressure in adult patients with acute hypotensive states.

Initial dose of 0.25 mL to 0.375 mL (from 8 mcg to 12 mcg of base) per minute, adjust the rate of flow to establish and maintain a low to normal blood pressure (usually 80 mm Hg to 100 mm Hg systolic) sufficient to maintain the circulation of vital organs.

For adults with septic shock, recommend norepinephrine as the first-line agent over other vasopressors and recommend an initial target mean arterial pressure (MAP) of 65 mmHg over higher MAP targets. regimens.dose_text: FDA label: Initiate at 8 to 12 mcg/min (0.25 to 0.375 mL/min of 4 mg/1000 mL dilution) and titrate to maintain low-normal BP (usually SBP 80-100 mmHg, or MAP >= 65 mmHg per SSC 2021); average maintenance 2 to 4 mcg/min (weight-based ICU titration typically 0.01 to 0.5+ mcg/kg/min). Correct occult hypovolemia prior to or during therapy.

regimens.indication: Neurocritical Care Hemodynamic Augmentation (Acute SCI MAP 85-90 mmHg / SAH DCI Induced HTN)

refs.quote: In acute traumatic cervical or thoracic spinal cord injury, avoid hypotension (SBP < 90 mmHg) and maintain MAP between 85 and 90 mmHg for the first 5 to 7 days post-injury to optimize spinal cord perfusion; norepinephrine is generally preferred over dopamine in cervical/high-thoracic SCI due to fewer arrhythmias and lower ICP effects. tier.note: 5-axis synthesis: Limited published human data at delivery have not identified an increased risk of major birth defects, but alpha-adrenergic uterine vasoconstriction can reduce uteroplacental perfusion; maternal hemodynamic stabilization in shock takes priority.

refs.quote: Limited published data consisting of a small number of case reports and multiple small trials involving the use of norepinephrine in pregnant women at the time of delivery have not identified an increased risk of major birth defects, miscarriage or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes.

In pregnant patients with septic, cardiogenic, or anaphylactic shock, maternal hemodynamic stabilization and restoration of uteroplacental perfusion take absolute priority; norepinephrine and epinephrine should not be withheld due to theoretical fetal concerns.

pregnancy_pk.value: No formal pregnancy PK dose-adjustment schedule; titrate to lowest effective dose maintaining maternal MAP >= 65 mmHg with continuous fetal heart rate monitoring when viable.

refs.quote: Because alpha-adrenergic vasoconstriction can reduce uterine blood flow, titrate to the lowest effective dose with continuous fetal heart rate monitoring when viable. lactation_summary.value: No data on human milk excretion; because norepinephrine has poor oral bioavailability and a 1 to 2 minute plasma half-life, clinically relevant infant exposure is not expected.

refs.quote: There are no data on the presence of norepinephrine in either human or animal milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or the effects on milk production. Clinically relevant exposure to the infant is not expected based on the short half-life and poor oral bioavailability of norepinephrine.

Because norepinephrine is poorly absorbed orally and has a short half-life, amounts ingested by the infant are expected to be negligible and destroyed in the gastrointestinal tract; however, intravenous norepinephrine is used in critically ill mothers where maternal stabilization is the primary consideration.
